title: Red Nichols's many recording groups
summary: They discuss Nichols recording on many labels, with Miff and the Charleston Chasers, Five Pennies and Redheads.

bands.name: Red Nichols and His Five Pennies

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Yes. Yes. Was Abe Lincoln of any importance in those years?

Well, he was playing with Nichols a lot. And was fine. Everybody thought the world of him. He was playing with the big society bands like Badouk was and some of the others. But he was also doing the little band work. Nichols was recording on 14 labels, I think, at that point. Yes. And the Mollers were always Miff and the Charleston Chasers, I think. And the Five Pennies tended to change a little bit.
The Redheads could be anybody. Could be Lannan's Redheads, in fact.
